items.title: Kimi K3 pushes open models forward
items.oneliner: Kimi K3 lands at 2.8 trillion parameters with multimodal support, raising the floor for serious open-weight model builders.

items.title: OpenAI ships new transcription models
items.oneliner: OpenAI's new transcription models support 57 languages, making real-time voice products easier to ship beyond English-only demos.

items.title: Agent intrusion became a real incident
items.oneliner: A frontier agent executed 17,600 actions over 2.5 days, proving autonomous intrusion is now an operational security problem.

items.title: Word documents can spread AI worms
items.oneliner: Researchers showed prompt-injected Word files can self-propagate through Copilot workflows, turning documents into active attack surfaces.

items.title: Claude found cryptographic weaknesses
items.oneliner: Claude helped uncover cryptographic weaknesses, a reminder that offensive security research is getting cheaper and faster with LLMs.

items.title: AI insiders are asking for pacing
items.oneliner: More than 1,000 AI lab staff backed frontier pacing, signaling safety concerns have moved from critics to builders.

items.title: AI data center debt is surging
items.oneliner: AI data-center bond issuance hit about $270 billion in 2026, putting real financing pressure behind every compute roadmap.

items.title: OpenAI released a security coding tool
items.oneliner: OpenAI's Codex Security gives teams an open-source CLI for finding and fixing repo vulnerabilities inside CI workflows.

items.title: Zig makes rebuilds nearly instant
items.oneliner: Zig 0.17.0 incremental compilation cuts rebuilds to roughly 50 to 70 milliseconds, which changes the feel of systems development.

items.title: Token optimization is now material
items.oneliner: One agent workflow cut token usage 8x and doubled speed, showing cost engineering is now a core product skill.
